title: Usability and Content Design
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of usability and content design and at least two listed subtopics.
Interpret the usability and content design example and predict its expected result.
Choose a verification step and identify one version, security, data, or troubleshooting consideration.

content.intro: Learn usability and content design through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Usability and Content Design matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines usability and content design as part of localization, accessibility, and user experience. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Helpful validation messages; Loading, success, and failure states; Accessible confirmations; Clear permission-denied pages; Recoverable user workflows. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Helpful validation messages
items.text: Helpful validation messages shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

items.title: Loading, success, and failure states
items.text: Treat Loading, success, and failure states as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

items.title: Accessible confirmations
items.text: Accessible confirmations is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Clear permission-denied pages
items.text: Clear permission-denied pages is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Recoverable user workflows
items.text: For Recoverable user workflows, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Usability and Content Design
content_blocks.code:
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _

label = _("Save changes")
content_blocks.expected_output: The label is marked for translation and can be mapped to a localized string in the configured locale.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First identify the input and the responsible Django component. Next trace how the example moves through “Usability and Content Design” and the related concept “Helpful validation messages”. Predict the result before running or inspecting it. Finally compare the observed behavior with the expected result and the cited official documentation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Helpful validation messages. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to describe usability and content design, explain the listed topics, inspect the example, and choose an appropriate verification step. Keep the scope and version caveat visible when sharing your solution.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a framework fragment without its imports, configuration, model, or URL context.
common_mistakes.why: The snippet may be incomplete when separated from a Django project.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the stated prerequisites and run the relevant management check or focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting input or relying only on a happy-path example.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid values, unauthorized requests, or concurrent activity can violate assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and add a negative or boundary test.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating the development sample as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Production hosting, secrets, storage, monitoring and resource limits differ from local use.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the current deployment/security references and document untested areas.
